abstract_sentences.text: Entropic optimal transport (EOT) via Sinkhorn iterations is widely used in modern machine learning, yet GPU solvers remain inefficient at scale.
abstract_sentences.transition: Introduces the application scope, then creates the systems-performance problem.

evidence.anchor: GPU solvers remain inefficient at scale.

abstract_sentences.text: Tensorized implementations suffer quadratic HBM traffic from dense n × m interactions, while existing online backends avoid storing dense matrices but still rely on generic tiled map-reduce reduction kernels with limited fusion.
abstract_sentences.transition: Splits the gap into the dense-traffic and generic-reduction mechanisms.

abstract_sentences.text: We present FlashSinkhorn, an IO-aware EOT solver for squared Euclidean cost that rewrites stabilized log-domain Sinkhorn updates as row-wise LogSumExp reductions of biased dot-product scores, the same normalization as transformer attention.
abstract_sentences.transition: Answers the bottleneck with an algebraic correspondence.

evidence.anchor: row-wise LogSumExp reductions of biased dot-product scores

abstract_sentences.text: This enables FlashAttention-style fusion and tiling: fused Triton kernels stream tiles through on-chip SRAM and update dual potentials in a single pass, substantially reducing HBM IO per iteration while retaining linear-memory operations.
abstract_sentences.transition: Turns the correspondence into a hardware dataflow mechanism.

abstract_sentences.text: We further provide streaming kernels for transport application, enabling scalable first- and second-order optimization.
abstract_sentences.transition: Extends the forward update to transport, gradient, and HVP uses.

abstract_sentences.text: On A100 GPUs, FlashSinkhorn achieves up to 32× forward-pass and 161× end-to-end speedups over state-of-the-art online baselines on point-cloud OT, improves scalability on OT-based downstream tasks.
abstract_sentences.transition: Supplies the abstract's strongest empirical claim after the mechanism.

evidence.anchor: up to 32× forward-pass and 161× end-to-end speedups

abstract_sentences.text: For reproducibility, we release an open-source implementation at https://github.com/ot-triton-lab/flash-sinkhorn.

abstract_summary.function_order: object_scope/problem_gap → split bottleneck → core idea/method → IO mechanism → derivative capability → quantitative result → reproducibility

equation_theory_inventory.label: Proposition 1
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Squared Euclidean cost; shifted potentials and precomputable biases.
equation_theory_inventory.conclusion: Each stabilized half-step is exactly a biased dot-product row-wise LSE.

evidence.anchor: Sinkhorn iteration as biased dot-product LSE

equation_theory_inventory.label: Theorem 2
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Tile fit condition and stated SRAM capacity regime.
equation_theory_inventory.conclusion: Algorithm 1 has the stated HBM-access bounds.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Proposition 3
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Any shifted potentials and transport matrix induced by them.
equation_theory_inventory.conclusion: PV and P-transpose U equal marginal-corrected row-softmax applications.

evidence.anchor: Transport matrix application as an attention output

equation_theory_inventory.label: Corollary 4
equation_theory_inventory.conclusion: Barycentric projection and gradient have the attention form.
equation_theory_inventory.empirical_counterpart: OTDD gradient flow and backward benchmarks.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Theorem 5
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Squared-Euclidean EOT; CG Schur solve over the optimal coupling.
equation_theory_inventory.conclusion: Streaming HVP uses specified transport applications with O((n+m)d) memory.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Lemma 6
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Optimal EOT coupling and squared Euclidean cost.
equation_theory_inventory.conclusion: Potential Jacobians solve the stated sensitivity linear system.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Theorem 7
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Squared Euclidean EOT and optimal coupling sensitivity.
equation_theory_inventory.conclusion: The data Hessian decomposes into an implicit R-transpose H-dagger R term and block-diagonal E.

result_inventory.claim: FlashSinkhorn reduces measured HBM traffic and runtime in the forward profiling setting.
result_inventory.value: At n=m=10,000,d=64,10 iterations: Flash 0.08 GB and 8.2 ms; KeOps 0.14 GB and 125.5 ms; Tensorized 98 GB and 54.0 ms.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Single NCU profiling table; no interval or hypothesis test reported.
result_inventory.adverse_explanation: Working set fits L2; Table 5 says HBM traffic reflects L2-resident execution.

evidence.anchor: Working set (5 MB) fits in A100 L2 cache

result_inventory.claim: Selected point-cloud forward and end-to-end benchmarks favor FlashSinkhorn over online baselines.
result_inventory.value: Table 3 reports forward 9.4–31.7x over KeOps and forward+backward up to 161x; JAX ratios reach 5.1x.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Mean timing across 50 forward and 30 backward repetitions; speedup is a ratio of timings; no variance/CI/test reported.
result_inventory.adverse_explanation: The selected table covers four n,d settings only; complete sweeps appear in Appendix H.

evidence.anchor: We report mean timing across repetitions.

result_inventory.claim: The method retains linear measured memory scaling and reaches large HVP settings.
result_inventory.value: Figure 3 reports O(n) memory; at n=m=50,000,d=64 Flash HVP is 4.2s versus KeOps 14.5s.
result_inventory.comparison: FlashSinkhorn versus Tensorized, KeOps, and OTT-JAX.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Descriptive log-scale line plots and OOM/OOT outcomes; no uncertainty band.
result_inventory.adverse_explanation: The conclusion is measured on A100-80GB and fixed benchmark settings.

result_inventory.claim: The OTDD kernel supports label-augmented cost at n=60,000 without tensorized memory growth.
result_inventory.value: Peak memory remains under 1 GB at n=60,000; Tensorized OOMs beyond n=20,000 in the stated comparison.
result_inventory.comparison: FlashSinkhorn versus Tensorized baseline on MNIST to Fashion-MNIST.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Single dataset-pair scaling curves; no uncertainty expression.
result_inventory.adverse_explanation: KeOps lacks the custom discrete W lookup, so the labelled comparison is not a three-way baseline test.

evidence.anchor: GeomLoss (KeOps) does not support custom cost functions

result_inventory.claim: Streaming HVP enables an Adam-to-Newton saddle-escape protocol in the shuffled regression task.
result_inventory.value: Across 72 random initializations, Adam escaped 71; post-escape Newton median was 11 steps. Figure 5 gives 2423s versus 2785s for one trajectory.
result_inventory.comparison: Adam plus Newton versus Adam continuation/only.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Failure count, median, and single-run wall-time plot; no CI/test reported.
result_inventory.adverse_explanation: The data correspondence and transformation are synthetically generated and lambda_min thresholding is a protocol choice.

result_inventory.claim: The damped streaming HVP approximately matches a dense Moore–Penrose reference.
result_inventory.value: Default relative error is 4.24–4.89e-3 for epsilon 0.10–0.50; at epsilon 0.01 it is 8.54e-3 with 195 CG iterations.
result_inventory.comparison: Streaming damped Schur-CG HVP versus dense reference.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Relative Frobenius error for stated configurations; no repeated-sample uncertainty.
result_inventory.adverse_explanation: Damping causes a bias floor and low epsilon increases conditioning cost.

result_inventory.claim: Tensorized implementation can win at very high dimension while retaining a memory disadvantage.
result_inventory.value: Table 10 gives 0.5–0.7 Flash/Tensorized speedup at d=1024; Table 11 gives 0.5–0.9.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Fixed-setting timing grid; values below one favor Tensorized.
result_inventory.adverse_explanation: The paper attributes the reversal to on-the-fly recomputation at large d.

result_inventory.claim: Low epsilon preserves approximately constant per-iteration forward time but needs more convergence iterations.
result_inventory.value: At epsilon 0.10/0.05/0.01 Flash is 7.75/7.81/7.60 ms for ten iterations; convergence budget rises 2000/4000/5000.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Descriptive timings and fixed precision comparison; no CI/test.
result_inventory.adverse_explanation: The total solve time grows because iteration budget grows, and HVP conditioning deteriorates.

evidence.anchor: Forward time in ms at low epsilon

claim_closure.evidence_response: Appendix D.1 gives the algebraic proof; Figure 1 depicts its dataflow.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion restates biased dot-product LSE execution.

claim_closure.claim: The row-stationary streaming implementation reduces HBM IO while preserving exact updates.
claim_closure.origin: Abstract sentence 4 and Introduction method preview, page 1.
claim_closure.method_response: Algorithm 1 fixes row blocks and maintains online LSE statistics.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Theorem 2 gives HBM bounds; Table 2 and Table 5–7 report profiler counters.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion states that the implementation avoids n by m materialization.

claim_closure.claim: The same streaming structure supports transport application, first-order gradients, and HVPs.
claim_closure.origin: Abstract sentence 5 and contribution list, pages 1–2.
claim_closure.method_response: Proposition 3, Corollary 4, and Theorem 5 provide the operation identities and HVP oracle.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 3, Table 14–16, and Figure 6 show HVP timings, parity, and memory.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion emphasizes EOT iteration, not detailed derivative claims.

claim_closure.claim: FlashSinkhorn yields up to 32x forward and 161x end-to-end speedup over online baselines.
claim_closure.method_response: Fused kernels implement the same update family as baseline schedules.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 3 and broad grids report speedup ratios, with timing means and profiler explanation.

evidence.anchor: We report mean timing across repetitions.

claim_closure.claim: FlashSinkhorn improves scalability of OT-based downstream tasks.
claim_closure.method_response: Custom label lookup and HVP make OTDD/optimization tasks executable without dense transport materialization.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 4 tests one OTDD dataset pair; Figure 5 tests one shuffled-regression construction plus 72 starts.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion asserts large-scale EOT becomes practical in the memory-bound regime.

claim_closure.claim: The fused streaming path applies to the squared-Euclidean/dot-product cost class.
claim_closure.method_response: Proposition 1's affine dot-product condition specifies the boundary.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Section 3.1 identifies raw Euclidean and learned neural costs as outside the form; Appendix grids give high-dimension and aspect-ratio boundaries.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion identifies non-dot-product costs as future work.

claim_closure.claim: The HVP enables reliable saddle-escape switching at lambda_min threshold 0.001.
claim_closure.method_response: Streaming HVP supplies Lanczos matvecs and the switch rule.
claim_closure.evidence_response: 72 random starts and one multi-saddle trajectory support the reported task; inexact damping/error remains.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion does not restate this downstream policy.

rhetorical_audit.text_scope: Heuristic scan of PDF pages 1–9 after removing repeated running headers; formula/table fragments can remain.
rhetorical_audit.qualifier_context: exact appears in algebra/theorem claims; substantially and up to anchor performance claims; can, may, and typically occur in scope and tradeoff statements.

final_judgment.single_storyline: For squared-Euclidean EOT, exact attention-form LSE algebra allows row-stationary Triton tiling that avoids n by m HBM intermediates, and the same structure extends to transport, gradients, and HVPs.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The bottleneck, core equations, Algorithms 1–2, Figure 1–5, Table 1–3, central theorem statements, two downstream tasks, and scope sentence remain in the nine-page main body.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Proofs, Algorithms 3–5, version/repetition details, profiler decomposition, full sweeps, low-epsilon/rectangular boundaries, HVP parity, OTDD preprocessing, and saddle protocol move to pages 13–36.
final_judgment.best_pattern: Build one measured systems causal chain: data-movement bottleneck, exact reparameterization, concrete dataflow, complexity statement, profiler counters, and workload consequences.
final_judgment.largest_gap: The paper lacks component-removal ablations, cross-GPU evidence, broad uncertainty reporting, and a compact main-text account of the large appendix's boundary results.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: When a systems method claims speed from structural reformulation, pair an exact or controlled derivation with counters that measure the proposed mechanism and with downstream evidence using the same operator.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This rule transfers when algebra and hardware make a shared bottleneck measurable; it does not license the same kernel path for costs without affine dot-product structure or regimes where dense GEMM is favorable.
